symptom: A layout created by mxcli whose placeholder is named anything but `Main` passes `mxcli check -p --references` AND `mxcli exec` ("Created layout"), then fails `mx check` with [CE0848] "No placeholder with the name 'Main' found. There should be exactly one." — and there is no DROP LAYOUT to undo it
cause: The write-time guard (`hasAnyPlaceholder`, mdl/backend/modelsdk/layout_write.go) asked only whether SOME placeholder existed, under any name. That was a faithful implementation of mxcli's own documented belief: CLAUDE.md and the layouts skill both said the name was a naming convention ("22 of 22 Atlas layouts follow it"). mxbuild validates it as a rule. Nothing between the author and the builder resolves a placeholder name, so check had no rule to apply either.
fix: Rule measured first, then written once: mdl/types/layout_placeholders.go `CheckLayoutPlaceholderNames`, applied by BOTH mdl/executor/validate_layout_placeholders.go (MDL081/MDL082, project-free pass) and the writer guard. Docs corrected in the same commit.
insight: The bug was a DOCUMENTED BELIEF, not an oversight — which is why grepping the code for a missing check would never have found it: the check that existed matched the docs exactly. When a guard looks deliberate and cites a rationale, verify the RATIONALE against the tool, not the guard against the rationale. One 10-minute measurement (create the layout, run mx check) overturned a sentence that had been carried in CLAUDE.md through several features. Measure against a layout NO PAGE USES, or you cannot tell a layout rule from a page-binding rule — here it errors unconditionally, which is what makes it checkable with no project.
controls: Five shapes on mxbuild 11.12.1: Main→0; Main+Content→0 (so extra names are fine, and a rule demanding all-Main would have been wrong); Content→CE0848; Main+Main→CE0849+CE0495; Main+Side+Side→CE0495 (so uniqueness is general, a second independent half of the rule).
